tools.name: agent
tools.description: Agent automation: move/turn/teleport agent, mine/place blocks, inventory management, item collection/dropping, block inspection. Perfect for automated building, resource gathering, exploration. Actions: move(forward/back/left/right), teleport(coordinates), mine_block(direction), place_block(slot+direction), get_inventory, collect_item, attack

steps.description: Array of agent actions for sequence. Each step should have "type" field and relevant parameters.

tools.name: blocks
tools.description: Block operations: single block placement, area filling, terrain analysis. Actions: set_block(single), fill_area(large_regions), get_top_solid_block(surface_level), query_block_data(block_info). Perfect for construction, terraforming, or analyzing terrain. Examples: set_block(x,y,z,stone), fill_area(x1,y1,z1 to x2,y2,z2,dirt), supports replace/keep/destroy modes

x2.description: Second X coordinate for area operations

y2.description: Second Y coordinate for area operations

z2.description: Second Z coordinate for area operations

steps.description: Array of block actions for sequence. Each step should have "type" field and relevant parameters.

tools.name: build_bezier
tools.description: Build BEZIER CURVE: smooth curved path, arch, bridge, decorative curve. Specify start point (startX,startY,startZ) + end point (endX,endY,endZ) + control points array. Control points define curve shape. 1 control point = quadratic curve (simple arch), 2+ control points = cubic/higher curves (complex shapes). Perfect for bridges, arches, decorative paths, roller coaster tracks.

startY.description: Start point Y coordinate (height of curve start)

endY.description: End point Y coordinate (height of curve end)

controlPoints.description: Control points that define curve shape. Array of {x, y, z} objects. 1 point = quadratic curve, 2 points = cubic curve, 3+ points = higher degree curves. Minimum 1, maximum 10 control points.

items.description: Control point with x, y, z coordinates

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, gold_block, quartz_block)

segments.description: Number of segments (more = smoother curve). Auto-calculated if not specified. Range: 10-1000

adaptive.description: Use adaptive segment calculation based on curve length (recommended for best results)

tools.name: build_cube
tools.description: Build CUBE/RECTANGLE: box, rectangle, wall, platform, room, house frame. Define with 2 corners (x1,y1,z1) to (x2,y2,z2). Coordinates can be positive or negative (e.g. x:-50, z:-100). Supports sequences for automation.

x1.description: Starting X coordinate (east-west, can be negative like -50)

y1.description: Starting Y coordinate (height, usually 64-100 for ground level)

z1.description: Starting Z coordinate (north-south, can be negative like -100)

x2.description: Ending X coordinate (east-west, can be negative)

y2.description: Ending Y coordinate (height, can be higher than y1 for tall structures)

z2.description: Ending Z coordinate (north-south, can be negative)

direction.description: Orientation direction: +x, +y, +z, -x, -y, -z, or custom for advanced rotation

tools.name: build_cylinder
tools.description: Build CYLINDER: tower, pillar, column, chimney, pipe, tube. Requires: centerX,centerY,centerZ,radius,height. Optional: axis

centerX.description: Center X coordinate (east-west position where the cylinder will be centered)

centerY.description: Bottom Y coordinate (ground level height where cylinder starts, typically 64)

centerZ.description: Center Z coordinate (north-south position where the cylinder will be centered)

radius.description: Radius in blocks (how wide the cylinder is). Thin: 2-4, Medium: 5-10, Wide: 15-30

height.description: Height in blocks (how tall the cylinder is). Short: 5-10, Medium: 15-25, Tall: 30-50

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, brick, concrete, wood, etc.)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for cylinder shell/walls only, or solid (false) for full cylinder

axis.description: Direction the cylinder extends: y=vertical (normal tower), x=horizontal east-west, z=horizontal north-south

tools.name: build_ellipsoid
tools.description: Build an ellipsoid (stretched/oval sphere) structure. Perfect for egg shapes, stretched domes, oval rooms, or artistic sculptures. Different radii create unique shapes. Example: radiusX=10, radiusY=5, radiusZ=10 creates a flattened dome

radiusX.description: Width radius (east-west stretch). Large=wide shape, Small=narrow shape. Example: 10=wide, 5=narrow

radiusY.description: Height radius (vertical stretch). Large=tall shape, Small=flat shape. Example: 15=tall dome, 3=flat pancake

radiusZ.description: Depth radius (north-south stretch). Large=deep shape, Small=shallow shape. Example: 8=deep, 4=shallow

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, glass, concrete, wool for colorful sculptures)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for shell/room inside, or solid (false) for full ellipsoid sculpture

tools.name: build_helix
tools.description: Build HELIX/SPIRAL: spiral staircase, corkscrew, DNA model, twisted tower. Requires: centerX,centerY,centerZ,radius,height,turns. Optional: axis,direction,chirality

radius.description: How wide the spiral is (distance from center). Small spiral=3, Medium=8, Large=15. Larger radius = wider staircases

height.description: How tall the spiral is (total vertical height). Short=10, Medium=25, Tall=50. Each turn uses height/turns blocks vertically

turns.description: How many complete rotations. Few turns=gentle slope (1-2), Many turns=steep spiral (5-10). 0.5=half turn, 1.5=one and half turns

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stairs for actual staircases, stone for pillars, glowstone for decorative spirals)

clockwise.description: Rotation direction: true=clockwise (right-hand spiral), false=counter-clockwise (left-hand spiral)

axis.description: Helix axis direction: x (east-west), y (up-down), z (north-south)

direction.description: Growth direction along axis: positive or negative

chirality.description: Helix handedness: right (clockwise from growth direction), left (counter-clockwise)

tools.name: build_hyperboloid
tools.description: Build HYPERBOLOID: cooling tower, hourglass, nuclear tower. Requires: centerX,centerY,centerZ,baseRadius,waistRadius,height. Optional: axis

centerX.description: Center X coordinate (east-west position of hyperboloid base center)

centerY.description: Center Y coordinate (height/vertical position of hyperboloid base, typically 64-100)

centerZ.description: Center Z coordinate (north-south position of hyperboloid base center)

baseRadius.description: Radius at the base in blocks. Small: 5-8, Medium: 10-15, Large: 20-30

waistRadius.description: Radius at the narrowest point (waist) in blocks. Should be smaller than baseRadius

height.description: Total height of the hyperboloid in blocks. Small: 10-15, Medium: 20-30, Large: 40-60

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, glass, wool, concrete, etc.)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for tower shell, or solid (false) for full hyperboloid

axis.description: Hyperboloid axis direction: x (east-west), y (up-down), z (north-south)

tools.name: build_line
tools.description: Build a straight line of blocks between two points. Perfect for paths, roads, fences, bridges, pillars, or structural frameworks. Example: from (0,64,0) to (10,80,10) creates a diagonal line useful for building supports or artistic structures

x1.description: Starting X coordinate (east-west position where line begins)

y1.description: Starting Y coordinate (height where line begins, typically 64 for ground level)

z1.description: Starting Z coordinate (north-south position where line begins)

x2.description: Ending X coordinate (east-west position where line ends)

y2.description: Ending Y coordinate (height where line ends, can be different for slopes/ramps)

z2.description: Ending Z coordinate (north-south position where line ends)

material.description: Block type to build the line with (e.g. stone, cobblestone, wood, concrete)

tools.name: build_paraboloid
tools.description: Build PARABOLOID: satellite dish, bowl, dish, parabolic. Requires: centerX,centerY,centerZ,radius,height. Optional: axis,direction

centerX.description: Center X coordinate (east-west position of paraboloid base center)

centerY.description: Center Y coordinate (height/vertical position of paraboloid base, typically 64-100)

centerZ.description: Center Z coordinate (north-south position of paraboloid base center)

radius.description: Maximum radius at the top of the paraboloid in blocks. Small: 3-5, Medium: 8-12, Large: 15-20

height.description: Height of the paraboloid in blocks. Small: 5-8, Medium: 10-15, Large: 20-30

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, glass, wool, concrete, etc.)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for dish shell, or solid (false) for full paraboloid

axis.description: Paraboloid axis direction: x (east-west), y (up-down), z (north-south)

direction.description: Opening direction: positive (opens toward +axis), negative (opens toward -axis)

tools.name: build_rotate
tools.description: Rotate and copy a structure around a pivot point. Perfect for creating rotated copies of buildings, making symmetrical structures, or spinning decorations. Example: rotate a house 90° around its center to create multiple orientations

axis.description: Rotation axis: y=spin horizontally (most common), x=tip forward/backward, z=roll left/right

angle.description: Rotation angle in degrees. Common angles: 90=quarter turn, 180=half turn, 270=three-quarter turn, 45=diagonal

material.description: Block type to build the rotated copy with (e.g. same as original, or different material for contrast)

tools.name: build_sphere
tools.description: Build SPHERE: ball, dome, round structure, planet, orb. Specify center (centerX,centerY,centerZ) + radius. Coordinates can be positive or negative (e.g. centerX:-25, centerZ:-75). Perfect for domes, decorations, planets, bubbles.

centerX.description: Center X coordinate (east-west position of sphere center)

centerY.description: Center Y coordinate (height/vertical position of sphere center, typically 64-100)

centerZ.description: Center Z coordinate (north-south position of sphere center)

radius.description: Radius of the sphere in blocks (how big the sphere is). Small: 3-5, Medium: 8-12, Large: 15-20

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone, glass, wool, concrete, etc.)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for sphere shell/dome, or solid (false) for full sphere

direction.description: Orientation direction: +x, +y, +z, -x, -y, -z, or custom for advanced rotation

tools.name: build_torus
tools.description: Build TORUS: donut, ring, circular fountain, arena seating, portal. Requires: centerX,centerY,centerZ,majorRadius,minorRadius. Optional: axis

majorRadius.description: Outer ring size (how big the overall donut is). Small ring=8, Medium ring=15, Large ring=30. This determines the donut hole size

minorRadius.description: Tube thickness (how thick the donut ring is). Thin tube=2, Medium tube=4, Thick tube=8. Must be smaller than majorRadius

material.description: Block type to build with (e.g. stone for foundations, glass for decorative rings, water for fountains)

hollow.description: Make it hollow (true) for ring shell only, or solid (false) for full torus structure

axis.description: Torus axis (normal to the plane): x (YZ-plane torus), y (XZ-plane torus), z (XY-plane torus)

tools.name: build_transform
tools.description: Transform structures by copying, rotating, mirroring, or scaling. Perfect for duplicating buildings, creating mirror images, or making scaled versions. Popular options: copy=duplicate, mirror_x=flip horizontally, scale_up=make 2x bigger

transformation.description: Transformation type: copy=exact duplicate, rotate_90/180/270=turn horizontally, mirror_x=flip east-west, mirror_y=flip up-down, mirror_z=flip north-south, scale_up=double size, scale_down=half size

material.description: Block type for the transformed structure (leave empty to copy original blocks, or specify material like stone, wood, etc.)

tools.name: camera
tools.description: CAMERA control: move_to (position camera), smooth_move (animated movement), track_entity (follow targets), fade (screen effects), reset (clear camera), set_mode (view presets). Supports both individual actions and cinematic sequences. Perfect for filming, showcasing builds, or creating camera movements. Requires cheats enabled.

action.description: Camera action: move_to=instant positioning, smooth_move=animated movement, track_entity=follow entities, fade=screen effects, reset=clear camera, set_mode=view presets/controls, sequence=cinematic camera sequences

entity.description: Entity selector to look at or track (@p=nearest player, @e=entities)

easing.description: Animation style: linear=constant, smooth=ease in/out, bounce=bouncy, elastic=springy

auto_clear.description: Automatically clear camera after action completes

shots.description: Array of camera shots for sequence action. Each shot executes after the previous one completes. Each shot object should have a "type" field (move_to, smooth_move, track_entity, fade, wait) plus relevant parameters like x,y,z coordinates, duration, etc.

tools.name: minecraft_wiki
tools.description: Search Minecraft Wiki for Bedrock Edition and Education Edition commands, blocks, items, entities, and game mechanics. Excludes Java Edition-only features. Returns accurate, up-to-date information from the official Minecraft Wiki. Use sequence action for step-by-step information gathering: 1) search for topic, 2) get specific page, 3) get detailed section - reduces overwhelming responses.

page_title.description: Specific wiki page title to retrieve

title.description: Wiki page title (alternative parameter name for compatibility)

section.description: Specific section name within a page

steps.description: Array of wiki search actions for sequence. Example: [{"type":"search","query":"give command","focus":"commands"},{"type":"get_page","title":"Commands/give"},{"type":"get_section","title":"Commands/give","section":"Syntax"}]. Use this to break down information gathering into manageable steps instead of getting overwhelming responses.

wait_time.description: Wait time in seconds after this step

tools.name: player
tools.description: PLAYER management: info/location/communication/inventory/abilities/gamemode. Actions: get_info/location (player details), send_message (chat to player), give_item (add to inventory), set_gamemode (survival/creative/adventure/spectator), add_levels (XP), get/set_ability (mayfly/mute/worldbuilder), get/check_tag, get_ping, list_all_players. Supports sequences for chained player operations.

action.description: Player operation to perform: get_info (returns player details), get_location (returns exact coordinates x,y,z including NEGATIVE values like x:-45.7, z:-123.2, plus rotation data), send_message (chat to player), give_item (add to inventory), set_gamemode (survival/creative/adventure/spectator), add_levels (XP), get/set_ability (mayfly/mute/worldbuilder), get/check_tag, get_ping, list_all_players. Use get_location before building to know exact position.

player_name.description: Target player name (optional, defaults to local player)

item_id.description: Item ID to give (e.g., minecraft:diamond, minecraft:iron_sword)

can_place_on.description: Blocks this item can be placed on (optional)

steps.description: Array of player sequence steps. Each step needs "type" (action) and params. Optional: "wait_time" (seconds), "on_error" (continue/stop/retry). Example: [{type:"send_message",message:"Hello!"},{type:"set_gamemode",gamemode:"creative",wait_time:1}]

type.description: Player action: get_info, get_location, send_message, give_item, set_gamemode, add_levels, get_abilities, set_ability, get_tags, check_tag, get_ping

wait_time.description: Seconds to wait after this step (0-60)

on_error.description: Error handling: continue (ignore), stop (halt), retry (try again)

tools.name: sequence
tools.description: Execute CROSS-TOOL SEQUENCES: Chain actions from multiple tools together with timing control. Perfect for complex automation like "teleport player → wait 2s → build cube → take screenshot → say message". Supports all tools: player(teleport/move/say), agent(move/turn), camera(shot/video), blocks(setblock/fill), world(time/weather), building(cube/sphere/line). Use wait_time for delays, on_error for handling failures.

steps.description: Array of sequence steps. Each step needs: "tool" (player/agent/camera/blocks/world/building), "type" (action like teleport/move/shot/setblock/build), and tool-specific params. Optional: "wait_time" (seconds to wait after), "on_error" (continue/stop/retry), "retry_count" (max retries). Example: [{tool:"player",type:"teleport",x:0,y:70,z:0,wait_time:2},{tool:"blocks",type:"setblock",x:0,y:70,z:0,block:"diamond_block"}]

tool.description: Tool name: player, agent, camera, blocks, world, or any building tool (build_cube, build_sphere, etc.)

type.description: Action type: depends on tool - player(teleport/move/say), agent(move/turn), camera(shot/video), blocks(setblock/fill), world(time/weather/gamemode), building(build)

wait_time.description: Seconds to wait after this step (default: 0)

on_error.description: Error handling: continue (ignore errors), stop (halt sequence), retry (try again)

description.description: Optional description of what this sequence does

tools.name: system
tools.description: System features: scoreboards (create/edit/delete objectives), screen displays (titles/subtitles/action_bars), player UI notifications. Actions: scoreboard_create/edit/delete, title_show(big_text), subtitle_show(small_text), actionbar_show(bottom_message). Perfect for displaying game stats, notifications, or creating UI elements

action.description: Action to perform within the category

player_name.description: Target player name (optional, defaults to local player)

steps.description: Array of system actions for sequence. Each step should have "category" and "action" fields and relevant parameters.

tools.name: world
tools.description: World management: control time/weather/environment. Actions: set_time(day/night/specific_time), set_weather(clear/rain/thunder), set_difficulty(peaceful/easy/normal/hard), set_spawn(coordinates), query_info(world_stats). Perfect for setting scene atmosphere, testing conditions, or creating specific environments. Examples: dawn=0, noon=6000, dusk=12000, midnight=18000

message.description: Message to send to all players

target.description: Target player for message (optional, defaults to all players)

command.description: Minecraft Bedrock Edition command to execute (without /). For correct syntax and available commands, use the minecraft_wiki tool to search for specific command information. Examples: "give @p diamond_sword", "tp @p 0 64 0", "setblock ~ ~ ~ stone"

steps.description: Array of world actions for sequence. Each step should have "type" field and relevant parameters.
